races.title: State Senate, District 2
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Norman Sanderson
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 2, in office since 2013 after one term in the NC House (2011-2013). Former Pamlico County sheriff's deputy, Christian school principal, and owner of a Havelock child care center for over 20 years. Studied at NC State; BA in Christian education from Logos.

controversies.text: Arrested Oct. 18, 2025 in Raleigh, where a breath test showed 0.16. On June 10, 2026 he pleaded guilty to driving while impaired. He got a suspended 30-day sentence and 12 months of unsupervised probation. The open-container and traffic-officer charges were dismissed. After the arrest he said, "Last night I made a regrettable mistake, and I take responsibility for my actions."

endorsements.text: His campaign site says he has been endorsed by the NRA since taking office and by Grassroots North Carolina (self-reported; not independently confirmed). Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or birth year. We found no stated position or documented action from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or slowing growth and protecting land. The bill sponsorship claims on his campaign site are his own statements and we could not confirm them in an independent record. The Ballotpedia list of bills he sponsored was empty in the page we read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His campaign site's "Meet Norman" page was cut off, and we did not read its Endorsements or Accomplishments pages.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he grew up on a family farm in Columbus County, NC, and that he and his wife have lived in Pamlico and Craven Counties for over 45 years; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the NC House (2011-2013) and NC Senate (2013-present), about 13 years of legislative service. Earlier worked as a sheriff's deputy and real estate business owner, and owned a child care center for over 20 years.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service, plus 20+ years as a small business owner who met a payroll and balanced a budget. Committee chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: Long prior legislative service, plus 20+ years as a small business owner who met a payroll and balanced a budget. Committee chair posts were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he supports the Second Amendment, is an NRA lifetime member, and has supported every gun rights bill in the General Assembly during his tenure.

workers-first.evidence: Says he was the original sponsor of a bill ordering NC sheriffs to note jail inmates' immigration status and assist federal agents who want to detain them.

pro-life.evidence: Says he believes in the sanctity of human life and co-sponsored the Heartbeat Bill and the Born-Alive Bill.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he believes parents should have the opportunity for school choice, and supports matching state funds for county teacher supplements in Tier 1 and Tier 2 counties.

back-police-order.evidence: Says it is important to support and fund law enforcement and other first responders.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 5 only promised

cands.name: Roy Surrett
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina Senate District 2 in 2026. He reports nearly four decades in the federal government: a U.S. Customs Officer, then a senior leader at the National Security Agency. He lives in Carteret County. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as receiving voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups: Better Future NC (Cam Pruette), Fair Map Fight Club, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Roy Surrett was born, or where he lived between college and his current Carteret County residence. We found no record of elected office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, guns, or abortion. His public safety statement is general and doesn't address pay, pensions or penalties. No controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond voter-guide groups were found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: About 38 years in federal service: U.S. Customs Officer, then NSA senior leader of multiple organizations. His campaign site says he managed complex budgets and handled sensitive foreign policy matters. No elected or legislative office is documented.
qual.why: A long management career with budget responsibility fits the middle band. There is no prior legislative service or local elected office, so he does not reach the high band.
